descriptors.concept_name: Environmental Management Accounting and Cost Control Summary
descriptors.definition: Environmental management accounting addresses the complex identification and allocation of environmental costs to prevent corporate financial harm and unsustainable business decisions. It operates alongside cost control mechanisms and target costing practices to drive permanent reductions in unit costs and foster proactive market-driven strategies.
inclusion: Identification and allocation of environmental costs
Comparison of actual costs with standards for cost regulation
Target costing approaches for market-driven pricing and profitability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard cost control mechanisms from proactive target costing techniques.
Separates environmental cost tracking from conventional financial accounting.
